657: fn get_payment_id(
658:     (metadata, payment_intent): (Option<Value>, Option<nexixpay::NexixpayPaymentIntent>),
659: ) -> CustomResult<String, errors::ConnectorError> {
660:     let connector_metadata = metadata.ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {
661:         field_name: "connector_meta",
662:     })?;
663:     let nexixpay_meta_data =
664:         serde_json::from_value::<nexixpay::NexixpayConnectorMetaData>(connector_metadata)
665:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::ParsingFailed)?;
666:     let payment_flow = payment_intent.unwrap_or(nexixpay_meta_data.psync_flow);
667:     let payment_id = match payment_flow {
668:         nexixpay::NexixpayPaymentIntent::Cancel => nexixpay_meta_data.cancel_operation_id,
669:         nexixpay::NexixpayPaymentIntent::Capture => nexixpay_meta_data.capture_operation_id,
670:         nexixpay::NexixpayPaymentIntent::Authorize => nexixpay_meta_data.authorization_operation_id,
671:     };
672:     payment_id.ok_or_else(|| {
673:         errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {
674:             field_name: "operation_id",
675:         }
676:         .into()
677:     })
678: }

<summary><h2> What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?</h2></summary>

Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in.

Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

<h3> Learn More About The Payment Modules </h3>
<details>

- **Cost Observability**  
  Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_

- **Revenue Recovery**  
  Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_

- **Vault**  
  A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_

- **Intelligent Routing**  
  Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_

- **Reconciliation**  
  Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_

- **Alternate Payment Methods**  
  Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_

</details>

```bash
cd hyperswitch

scripts/setup.sh
```
<details>

  - Offers multiple deployment profiles:
    - **Standard**: App server + Control Center  
    - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers  
    - **Minimal**: Standalone App server  
  - Provides access links when done

  If you need further help, check out our [video tutorial](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/overview/unified-local-setup-using-docker).  

  👉 After setup, [configure a connector](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/using-hyperswitch-control-center#add-a-payment-processor) and [test a payment](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/test-a-payment).

## Why Hyperswitch?

Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations.

Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are.

<strong>“Linux for Payments”</strong> — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack.

We believe in:

- <strong> Embracing Payment Diversity:</strong> Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows.

- <strong> Open Source by Default:</strong> Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software.

- <strong> Community-Driven Development:</strong> Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. 

- <strong> Systems-Level Engineering:</strong> We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance.

- <strong> Maximizing Value Creation:</strong> For developers, customers, and partners alike.

- <strong> Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested:</strong> Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide.

102: fn get_validated_address_details_generic<RouterContextDataAlias, AddressOutput>(
103:     data: &RouterContextDataAlias,
104:     address_kind: AddressKind,
105: ) -> Result<Option<AddressOutput>, error_stack::Report<errors::ConnectorError>>
106: where
107:     RouterContextDataAlias: crate::utils::RouterData,
108:     AddressOutput: AddressConstructor + Sized,
109: {
110:     let (
111:         opt_line1,
112:         opt_line2,
113:         opt_full_name,
114:         opt_city,
115:         opt_zip,
116:         opt_country,
117:         has_address_details_check,
118:         address_type_str,
119:         max_name_len,
120:         max_street_len,
121:         max_city_len,
122:         max_post_code_len,
123:         max_country_len,
124:     ) = match address_kind {
125:         AddressKind::Billing => (
126:             data.get_optional_billing_line1(),
127:             data.get_optional_billing_line2(),
128:             data.get_optional_billing_full_name(),
129:             data.get_optional_billing_city(),
130:             data.get_optional_billing_zip(),
131:             data.get_optional_billing_country()
132:                 .map(CountryAlpha2::from_alpha2_to_alpha3),
133:             data.get_optional_billing().is_some(),
134:             "billing",
135:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_NAME_LENGTH,
136:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_STREET_LENGTH,
137:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_CITY_LENGTH,
138:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_POST_CODE_LENGTH,
139:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_COUNTRY_LENGTH,
140:         ),
141:         AddressKind::Shipping => (
142:             data.get_optional_shipping_line1(),
143:             data.get_optional_shipping_line2(),
144:             data.get_optional_shipping_full_name(),
145:             data.get_optional_shipping_city(),
146:             data.get_optional_shipping_zip(),
147:             data.get_optional_shipping_country()
148:                 .map(CountryAlpha2::from_alpha2_to_alpha3),
149:             data.get_optional_shipping().is_some(),
150:             "shipping",
151:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_NAME_LENGTH,
152:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_STREET_LENGTH,
153:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_CITY_LENGTH,
154:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_POST_CODE_LENGTH,
155:             MAX_BILLING_ADDRESS_COUNTRY_LENGTH,
156:         ),
157:     };
158: 
159:     let street_val = match (opt_line1.clone(), opt_line2.clone()) {
160:         (Some(l1), Some(l2)) => Some(Secret::new(format!("{}, {}", l1.expose(), l2.expose()))),
161:         (Some(l1), None) => Some(l1),
162:         (None, Some(l2)) => Some(l2),
163:         (None, None) => None,
164:     };
165: 
166:     if has_address_details_check {
167:         let name_val = opt_full_name;
168:         if let Some(ref val) = name_val {
169:             let length = val.clone().expose().len();
170:             if length > max_name_len {
171:                 return Err(error_stack::Report::from(
172:                     errors::ConnectorError::MaxFieldLengthViolated {
173:                         field_name: format!(
174:                             "{address_type_str}.address.first_name & {address_type_str}.address.last_name",
175: 
176:                         ),
177:                         connector: "Nexixpay".to_string(),
178:                         max_length: max_name_len,
179:                         received_length: length,
180:                     },
181:                 ));
182:             }
183:         }
184: 
185:         if let Some(ref val) = street_val {
186:             let length = val.clone().expose().len();
187:             if length > max_street_len {
188:                 return Err(error_stack::Report::from(
189:                     errors::ConnectorError::MaxFieldLengthViolated {
190:                         field_name: format!(
191:                             "{address_type_str}.address.line1 & {address_type_str}.address.line2",
192:                         ),
193:                         connector: "Nexixpay".to_string(),
194:                         max_length: max_street_len,
195:                         received_length: length,
196:                     },
197:                 ));
198:             }
199:         }
200: 
201:         let city_val = opt_city;
202:         if let Some(ref val) = city_val {
203:             let length = val.len();
204:             if length > max_city_len {
205:                 return Err(error_stack::Report::from(
206:                     errors::ConnectorError::MaxFieldLengthViolated {
207:                         field_name: format!("{address_type_str}.address.city"),
208:                         connector: "Nexixpay".to_string(),
209:                         max_length: max_city_len,
210:                         received_length: length,
211:                     },
212:                 ));
213:             }
214:         }
215: 
216:         let post_code_val = opt_zip;
217:         if let Some(ref val) = post_code_val {
218:             let length = val.clone().expose().len();
219:             if length > max_post_code_len {
220:                 return Err(error_stack::Report::from(
221:                     errors::ConnectorError::MaxFieldLengthViolated {
222:                         field_name: format!("{address_type_str}.address.zip"),
223:                         connector: "Nexixpay".to_string(),
224:                         max_length: max_post_code_len,
225:                         received_length: length,
226:                     },
227:                 ));
228:             }
229:         }
230: 
231:         let country_val = opt_country;
232:         if let Some(ref val) = country_val {
233:             let length = val.to_string().len();
234:             if length > max_country_len {
235:                 return Err(error_stack::Report::from(
236:                     errors::ConnectorError::MaxFieldLengthViolated {
237:                         field_name: format!("{address_type_str}.address.country"),
238:                         connector: "Nexixpay".to_string(),
239:                         max_length: max_country_len,
240:                         received_length: length,
241:                     },
242:                 ));
243:             }
244:         }
245:         Ok(Some(AddressOutput::new(
246:             name_val,
247:             street_val,
248:             city_val,
249:             post_code_val,
250:             country_val,
251:         )))
252:     } else {
253:         Ok(None)
254:     }
255: }

514:         capture_operation_id: {

### How Hyperswitch handles 3DS redirect completion

#### 1. Core Trait Pattern
The `PaymentsCompleteAuthorize` trait is an empty marker trait that extends `ConnectorIntegration<CompleteAuthorize, CompleteAuthorizeData, PaymentsResponseData>`:

```rust
// crates/hyperswitch_interfaces/src/api/payments.rs:176-180
pub trait PaymentsCompleteAuthorize:
    api::ConnectorIntegration<CompleteAuthorize, CompleteAuthorizeData, PaymentsResponseData>
{}
```

In every connector, you declare:
```rust
impl api::PaymentsCompleteAuthorize for Worldpay {}
```

Then implement the full `ConnectorIntegration` with standard methods: `get_headers`, `get_url`, `get_request_body`, `build_request`, `handle_response`, `get_error_response`.

#### 2. Redirect Data Structures
The request data carries redirect data in `CompleteAuthorizeData`:

```rust
// crates/hyperswitch_domain_models/src/router_request_types.rs:817-855
pub struct CompleteAuthorizeData {
    pub redirect_response: Option<CompleteAuthorizeRedirectResponse>,
    pub connector_transaction_id: Option<String>,
    pub minor_amount: MinorUnit,
    pub currency: storage_enums::Currency,
    // ...other fields
}

pub struct CompleteAuthorizeRedirectResponse {
    pub params: Option<Secret<String>>,       // URL-encoded query string from redirect
    pub payload: Option<pii::SecretSerdeValue>, // JSON body from redirect
}
```

This is populated in two places:
- **Incoming request parsing**: `payment_complete_authorize.rs:242-245` extracts `request.feature_metadata.redirect_response`
- **Router data construction**: `transformers.rs:6031-6036` maps it into `CompleteAuthorizeRedirectResponse { params, payload }`

---

### Example 1: Worldpay — URL-encoded params with status-driven URL

**File**: `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/worldpay.rs` (lines 795-905)

Worldpay extracts `params` from `redirect_response`, deserializes it as URL-encoded data, and chooses the API endpoint based on the current `AttemptStatus`:

```rust
// transformers.rs:893-927
impl TryFrom<&types::PaymentsCompleteAuthorizeRouterData> for WorldpayCompleteAuthorizationRequest {
    fn try_from(item: &types::PaymentsCompleteAuthorizeRouterData) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        let params = item
            .request
            .redirect_response
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|r| r.params.as_ref())
            .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::ResponseDeserializationFailed)?;

        let parsed_request = serde_urlencoded::from_str::<Self>(params.peek())
            .change_context(...)?;

        match item.status {
            enums::AttemptStatus::DeviceDataCollectionPending => Ok(parsed_request),
            enums::AttemptStatus::AuthenticationPending => {
                if parsed_request.collection_reference.is_some() {
                    return Err(...); // validation guard
                }
                Ok(parsed_request)
            }
            _ => Err(...),
        }
    }
}
```

The URL itself is dynamic:
```rust
// worldpay.rs:811-837
let stage = match req.status {
    AttemptStatus::DeviceDataCollectionPending => "3dsDeviceData",
    AttemptStatus::AuthenticationPending => "3dsChallenges",
    _ => return Err(...),
};
Ok(format!("{}api/payments/{connector_payment_id}/{stage}", ...))
```

**Key pattern**: Use `serde_urlencoded::from_str` on `params.peek()` and vary behavior by `AttemptStatus`.

---

### Example 2: Cybersource — JSON payload extraction with preprocessing flow routing

**File**: `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/cybersource.rs` (lines 1610-1698)

Cybersource reads the **JSON payload** from `redirect_response.payload`, validates card data, and injects the 3DS `authentication_transaction_id`:

```rust
// transformers.rs:3764-3799
let redirect_response = item.router_data.request.redirect_response.clone().ok_or(...)?;

let redirect_payload: CybersourceRedirectionAuthResponse = redirect_response
    .payload
    .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::MissingConnectorRedirectionPayload { ... })?
    .peek()
    .clone()
    .parse_value("CybersourceRedirectionAuthResponse")
    .change_context(...)?;

// Build the request with the extracted transaction ID
Ok(Self {
    consumer_authentication_information:
        CybersourceConsumerAuthInformationValidateRequest {
            authentication_transaction_id: redirect_payload.transaction_id,
        },
    ...
})
```

Cybersource also supports **preprocessing flow selection** based on what the redirect contains:

```rust
// cybersource.rs:2282-2304
fn get_preprocessing_flow_if_needed(
    &self,
    current_flow_info: api::CurrentFlowInfo<'_>,
) -> Option<api::PreProcessingFlowName> {
    match current_flow_info {
        api::CurrentFlowInfo::CompleteAuthorize { request_data, .. } => {
            let redirect_response = request_data.redirect_response.as_ref()?;
            match redirect_response.params.as_ref() {
                Some(param) if !param.peek().is_empty() => {
                    Some(api::PreProcessingFlowName::Authenticate)
                }
                Some(_) | None => Some(api::PreProcessingFlowName::PostAuthenticate),
            }
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

**Key pattern**: Parse JSON payload with `parse_value(...)` and optionally branch preprocessing flows based on redirect content.

---

### Example 3: Bluesnap — Using both params and payload

**File**: `crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/bluesnap.rs` (lines 818-906)

Bluesnap uses **both** `params` (to extract the payment token) and `payload` (to extract 3DS authentication result):

```rust
// transformers.rs:604-682
let redirection_response: BluesnapRedirectionResponse = item
    .router_data
    .request
    .redirect_response
    .as_ref()
    .and_then(|res| res.payload.to_owned())
    .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::MissingConnectorRedirectionPayload { ... })?
    .parse_value("BluesnapRedirectionResponse")
    .change_context(...)?;

let token = item
    .router_data
    .request
    .redirect_response
    .clone()
    .and_then(|res| res.params.to_owned())
    .ok_or(...)
    .peek()
    .split_once('=')
    .ok_or(...)?.1
    .to_string();

let redirection_result: BluesnapThreeDsResult = redirection_response
    .authentication_response
    .parse_struct("BluesnapThreeDsResult")
    .change_context(...)?;

Ok(BluesnapCompletePaymentsRequest {
    pf_token: Secret::new(token),
    three_d_secure: Some(BluesnapThreeDSecureInfo {
        three_d_secure_reference_id: redirection_result
            .three_d_secure
            .ok_or(...)?.three_d_secure_reference_id,
    }),
    ...
})
```

**Key pattern**: Extract `params` for simple token/key-value data, and `payload` for structured JSON 3DS results.

---

### Summary of Redirect Payload Access Patterns

| Connector | Field Used | Parsing Method | Use Case |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|----------|
| **Worldpay** | `params` | `serde_urlencoded::from_str` | URL-encoded 3DS device/challenge data |
| **Cybersource** | `payload` | `parse_value("...")` | JSON `transaction_id` for consumer auth |
| **Bluesnap** | `params` + `payload` | `split_once('=')` + `parse_struct` | Token from params, 3DS result from payload |
| **NMI** | `payload` | `serde_json::from_value` | `cavv`, `xid`, `eci`, `directory_server_id` |

All connectors follow the same structural pattern:
1. Declare `impl api::PaymentsCompleteAuthorize for Connector {}`
2. Implement `ConnectorIntegration<CompleteAuthorize, CompleteAuthorizeData, PaymentsResponseData>`
3. In `get_request_body`, call `TryFrom<&PaymentsCompleteAuthorizeRouterData>` in the connector's transformers
4. Inside the transformer, access `item.router_data.request.redirect_response` to pull `params` or `payload`
5. Validate and map the redirect data into the connector-specific request struct

</answer>

<next_steps>

- Ready to proceed — no follow-up needed. Use the three examples above as templates for implementing 3DS redirect completion in a new connector.
- If you need the full flow for a specific connector (e.g., Adyen, Trustpay, or a newer one), search within `/crates/hyperswitch_connectors/src/connectors/<name>/transformers.rs` for `PaymentsCompleteAuthorizeRouterData` to see its redirect handling.
- To add a new connector's `CompleteAuthorize` flow, copy the trait impl + `ConnectorIntegration` boilerplate from any of the listed files and adapt the transformer to extract the redirect fields your connector expects.

</next_steps>
</results>

Based on my analysis of the official Nexixpay documentation and the hyperswitch connector implementation, here's everything you need to know about Nexixpay's 3D Secure payment completion API:

## 1. API Endpoints (3-Step Server-to-Server Flow)

### Step 1: Initialize 3DS Authentication
- **Endpoint**: `POST /orders/3steps/init`
- **Base URLs**:
  - **Production**: `https://xpay.nexigroup.com/api/phoenix-0.0/psp/api/v1/orders/3steps/init`
  - **Test**: `https://xpaysandbox.nexigroup.com/api/phoenix-0.0/psp/api/v1/orders/3steps/init`
- **Purpose**: Verify card enrollment and initiate 3D Secure
- **Returns**: `threeDSAuthUrl`, `ThreeDsRequest` code, and `operationId`

### Step 2: Validate 3DS Authentication Result
- **Endpoint**: `POST /orders/3steps/validation`
- **Purpose**: Validate the 3DS authentication outcome after redirect
- **Returns**: Authentication data (CAVV, ECI, XID) needed for payment

### Step 3: Complete Payment
- **Endpoint**: `POST /orders/3steps/payment`
- **Purpose**: Execute the actual payment authorization

---

## 2. Redirect Form Construction (Step 1 → Step 2)

After calling `/orders/3steps/init`, construct and submit a POST form to redirect the customer:

```html
<form name="redirect" action="<%=threeDSAuthUrl%>" method="POST">
  <input type="hidden" name="ThreeDsRequest" value="<%=ThreeDsRequest%>" />
  <input type="hidden" name="ReturnUrl" value="<%=ReturnUrl%>" />
  <input type="hidden" name="transactionId" value="<%=operationId%>" />
</form>
```

**Form Fields:**
| Field | Source | Description |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| `threeDSAuthUrl` | Response from `/orders/3steps/init` | ACS URL for authentication |
| `ThreeDsRequest` | Response from `/orders/3steps/init` | Auth request token |
| `ReturnUrl` | Merchant configured | Where customer returns after auth |
| `transactionId` | Response from `/orders/3steps/init` (operationId) | Transaction identifier |

---

## 3. Fields Returned from 3DS Redirect (Step 2)

When the customer completes 3D Secure, they are redirected back to your `ReturnUrl` with these parameters:

| Field | Description | Format |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| **`PaRes`** (or `PARes`) | Encrypted 3DS authentication result | String |
| **`MD`** | Payment session identifier (matches operationId) | String |
| **`paymentId`** | Same as operationId/MD | String |

**Example redirect payload:**
```json
{
  "PaRes": "encrypted_authentication_result_here",
  "paymentId": "3470744"
}
```

---

## 4. Validation Request (POST /orders/3steps/validation)

### Request Body
```json
{
  "operationId": "3470744",
  "threeDSAuthResponse": "ni2178hiekh29830..."
}
```

**Required Headers:**
- `X-Api-Key`: `625b4884-38f8-11ed-a261-0242ac120002` (UUID format)
- `Correlation-Id`: `4935e818-38e0-11ed-a261-0242ac120002` (UUID format)

---

## 5. Validation Response Fields

### Success Response (200)
```json
{
  "operation": {
    "orderId": "btid2384983",
    "operationId": "3470744",
    "operationResult": "THREEDS_VALIDATED",
    "threeDSAuthResult": {
      "authenticationValue": "AAIBBjhkYQAAAAAKl4FHdAAAAAA=",
      "cavvAlgorithm": "...",
      "eci": "05",
      "merchantAcquirerBin": "494330",
      "xid": "RExDQXMtS05EJTt6VlBNRnxdOkY=",
      "status": "VALIDATED",
      "version": "2.1.0"
    }
  }
}
```

**Key response fields:**
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `operationResult` | `THREEDS_VALIDATED`, `THREEDS_FAILED`, `AUTHORIZED`, etc. |
| `authenticationValue` | CAVV value for payment step |
| `eci` | Electronic Commerce Indicator |
| `xid` | Transaction identifier |
| `status` | `VALIDATED` or failure reason |

---

## 6. Hyperswitch Implementation Reference

From the current connector implementation, the key types used for 3DS handling are:

```rust
// Redirect payload received from 3DS ACS
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct RedirectPayload {
    #[serde(rename = "PaRes")]
    pub pa_res: Option<Secret<String>>,
    
    #[serde(rename = "paymentId")]
    pub payment_id: Option<String>,
}

// Validation request
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct NexixpayPreProcessingRequest {
    pub operation_id: Option<String>,
    pub three_d_s_auth_response: Option<Secret<String>>,
}

// Validation response
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct NexixpayPreProcessingResponse {
    pub operation: Operation,
    pub three_d_s_auth_result: ThreeDSAuthResult,
}

// 3DS auth result containing CAVV
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ThreeDSAuthResult {
    pub authentication_value: Option<Secret<String>>,
}
```

---

## 7. Complete Payment Request (Step 3)

For the final payment step, include the 3DS authentication data:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct NexixpayCompleteAuthorizeRequest {
    pub order: Order,
    pub card: NexixpayCard,
    pub operation_id: String,
    pub capture_type: Option<NexixpayCaptureType>,
    pub three_d_s_auth_data: ThreeDSAuthData,
    // ...
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ThreeDSAuthData {
    pub three_d_s_auth_response: Option<Secret<String>>,  // PaRes
    pub authentication_value: Option<Secret<String>>,      // CAVV from validation
}
```

---

## 8. Connector Metadata Storage

The hyperswitch connector stores intermediate state in `connector_metadata`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct NexixpayConnectorMetaData {
    pub three_d_s_auth_result: Option<ThreeDSAuthResult>,
    pub three_d_s_auth_response: Option<Secret<String>>,
    pub authorization_operation_id: Option<String>,
    pub capture_operation_id: Option<String>,
    pub psync_flow: NexixpayPaymentIntent,
}
```

---

## 9. Official Documentation Links

- **[3 Steps Payment Integration Guide](https://developer.nexi.it/en/modalita-di-integrazione/server-to-server/pagamento-3-steps)**
- **[POST /orders/3steps/init API](https://developer.nexi.it/en/api/post-orders-3steps-init)**
- **[POST /orders/3steps/validation API](https://developer.nexi.it/en/api/post-orders-3steps-validation)**
- **[Nexi XPay Global API Reference](https://developer.nexigroup.com/xpayglobal/en-EU/api/)**

---

## 10. Complete Flow Summary

| Step | Action | Endpoint | Input | Output |
|------|--------|----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Initiate 3DS | `POST /orders/3steps/init` | Card details, order info | `threeDSAuthUrl`, `ThreeDsRequest`, `operationId` |
| 2 | Redirect customer | POST form | `threeDSAuthUrl` + params | Customer authenticates with bank |
| 3 | Handle return | Receive redirect | `PaRes`, `paymentId` | Auth result encrypted |
| 4 | Validate 3DS | `POST /orders/3steps/validation` | `operationId`, `threeDSAuthResponse` (PaRes) | `authenticationValue` (CAVV), `eci`, `xid` |
| 5 | Complete payment | `POST /orders/3steps/payment` | Card data + 3DS auth data | Final payment result |

This information provides the complete picture for implementing Nexixpay 3DS redirect handling in the hyperswitch connector.

131:     fn get_auth_header(
132:         &self,
133:         auth_type: &ConnectorAuthType,
134:     ) -> CustomResult<Vec<(String, masking::Maskable<String>)>, errors::ConnectorError> {
135:         let auth = nexixpay::NexixpayAuthType::try_from(auth_type)
136:             .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::FailedToObtainAuthType)?;
137:         Ok(vec![
138:             (
139:                 headers::X_API_KEY.to_string(),
140:                 auth.api_key.expose().into_masked(),
141:             ),
142:             (
143:                 headers::CORRELATION_ID.to_string(),
144:                 Uuid::new_v4().to_string().into_masked(),
145:             ),
146:         ])
147:     }

149:     fn build_error_response(
150:         &self,
151:         res: Response,
152:         event_builder: Option<&mut ConnectorEvent>,
153:     ) -> CustomResult<ErrorResponse, errors::ConnectorError> {
154:         let response: nexixpay::NexixpayErrorResponse = match res.status_code {
155:             401 => nexixpay::NexixpayErrorResponse {
156:                 errors: vec![nexixpay::NexixpayErrorBody {
157:                     code: Some(consts::NO_ERROR_CODE.to_string()),
158:                     description: Some("UNAUTHORIZED".to_string()),
159:                 }],
160:             },
161:             404 => nexixpay::NexixpayErrorResponse {
162:                 errors: vec![nexixpay::NexixpayErrorBody {
163:                     code: Some(consts::NO_ERROR_CODE.to_string()),
164:                     description: Some("NOT FOUND".to_string()),
165:                 }],
166:             },
167:             _ => res
168:                 .response
169:                 .parse_struct("NexixpayErrorResponse")
170:                 .change_context(errors::ConnectorError::ResponseDeserializationFailed)?,
171:         };
172: 
173:         let concatenated_descriptions: Option<String> = {
174:             let descriptions: Vec<String> = response
175:                 .errors
176:                 .iter()
177:                 .filter_map(|error| error.description.as_ref())
178:                 .cloned()
179:                 .collect();
180: 
181:             if descriptions.is_empty() {
182:                 None
183:             } else {
184:                 Some(descriptions.join(", "))
185:             }
186:         };
187: 
188:         event_builder.map(|i| i.set_response_body(&response));
189:         router_env::logger::info!(connector_response=?response);
190: 
191:         Ok(ErrorResponse {
192:             status_code: res.status_code,
193:             code: response
194:                 .errors
195:                 .first()
196:                 .and_then(|error| error.code.clone())
197:                 .unwrap_or(consts::NO_ERROR_CODE.to_string()),
198:             message: response
199:                 .errors
200:                 .first()
201:                 .and_then(|error| error.description.clone())
202:                 .unwrap_or(consts::NO_ERROR_MESSAGE.to_string()),
203:             reason: concatenated_descriptions,
204:             attempt_status: None,
205:             connector_transaction_id: None,
206:             network_advice_code: None,
207:             network_decline_code: None,
208:             network_error_message: None,
209:             connector_metadata: None,
210:         })
211:     }
212: }

<summary><h2> What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?</h2></summary>

Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in.

Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

<h3> Learn More About The Payment Modules </h3>
<details>

- **Cost Observability**  
  Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_

- **Revenue Recovery**  
  Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_

- **Vault**  
  A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_

- **Intelligent Routing**  
  Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_

- **Reconciliation**  
  Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_

- **Alternate Payment Methods**  
  Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_

</details>

## Why Hyperswitch?

Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations.

Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are.

<strong>“Linux for Payments”</strong> — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack.

We believe in:

- <strong> Embracing Payment Diversity:</strong> Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows.

- <strong> Open Source by Default:</strong> Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software.

- <strong> Community-Driven Development:</strong> Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. 

- <strong> Systems-Level Engineering:</strong> We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance.

- <strong> Maximizing Value Creation:</strong> For developers, customers, and partners alike.

- <strong> Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested:</strong> Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide.

564:                     max_length: MAX_ORDER_ID_LENGTH,

566:                 },
567:             ))
568:         }
569:     } else {
570:         Ok(payment_id.to_string())
571:     }
572: }

779:     fn try_from(
780:         item: &NexixpayRouterData<&PaymentsAuthorizeRouterData>,

782:         match item
783:             .router_data
784:             .request
785:             .mandate_id
786:             .clone()
787:             .and_then(|mandate_id| mandate_id.mandate_reference_id)
788:         {
789:             None => {
790:                 let recurrence_request_obj = if item.router_data.request.is_mandate_payment() {
791:                     let contract_id = item
792:                         .router_data
793:                         .connector_mandate_request_reference_id
794:                         .clone()
795:                         .ok_or_else(|| errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {
796:                             field_name: "connector_mandate_request_reference_id",
797:                         })?;
798:                     RecurrenceRequest {
799:                         action: NexixpayRecurringAction::ContractCreation,
800:                         contract_id: Some(Secret::new(contract_id)),
801:                         contract_type: Some(ContractType::MitUnscheduled),
802:                     }
803:                 } else {
804:                     RecurrenceRequest {
805:                         action: NexixpayRecurringAction::NoRecurring,
806:                         contract_id: None,
807:                         contract_type: None,
808:                     }
809:                 };
810: 
811:                 match item.router_data.request.payment_method_data {
812:                     PaymentMethodData::Card(ref req_card) => {
813:                         if item.router_data.is_three_ds() {
814:                             Ok(Self::NexixpayNonMandatePaymentRequest(Box::new(
815:                                 NexixpayNonMandatePaymentRequest {

819:                                         cvv: req_card.card_cvc.clone(),
820:                                     },
821:                                     recurrence: recurrence_request_obj,
822:                                     action_type: if item.router_data.request.minor_amount
823:                                         == MinorUnit::zero()
824:                                     {
825:                                         Some(NexixpayPaymentRequestActionType::Verify)
826:                                     } else {
827:                                         None
828:                                     },
829:                                 },
830:                             )))
831:                         } else {
832:                             Err(errors::ConnectorError::NotSupported {
833:                                 message: "No threeds is not supported".to_string(),
834:                                 connector: "nexixpay",
835:                             }
836:                             .into())
837:                         }
838:                     }
839:                     PaymentMethodData::CardRedirect(_)
840:                     | PaymentMethodData::Wallet(_)
841:                     | PaymentMethodData::PayLater(_)
842:                     | PaymentMethodData::BankRedirect(_)
843:                     | PaymentMethodData::BankDebit(_)
844:                     | PaymentMethodData::BankTransfer(_)
845:                     | PaymentMethodData::Crypto(_)
